steps.question: Which color roles does it need?
steps.why: Brand accents are part of the message.

steps.pick: neutral.0: the base for content; body text reads 18.0:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.50: the base for content; body text reads 17.12:1 on it, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
steps.pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.26:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.69:1, on surface.default). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.

steps.pick: radius.24: Cards, menus and dialogs take a big, round 24px corner, so a card feels like a friendly object and keeps its box shape.

steps.question: How big are icons next to text?
steps.why: Larger icons hold their own next to big type.

steps.question: Which text roles does it need?
steps.why: A big expressive display role carries the brand.
A word keeps meaning on vivid backgrounds.

steps.pick: neutral.900: the strongest text step, 18.0:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.900: the strongest text step, 17.12:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.question: Which text roles does it need?
steps.why: A big expressive display role carries the brand.

steps.question: Where do the words matter most?
steps.why: Words work hardest in headlines and buttons.

steps.pick: neutral.600: the quietest text that still reads, 7.02:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.400: the quietest text that still reads, 6.71:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.question: Which color roles does it need?
steps.why: Brand accents are part of the message.

steps.question: What is a costly mistake?
steps.why: A bland page is the costly mistake.
Errors must not look like the brand.

steps.use: Plain first, a light touch after
steps.why: Playful copy must never hide what went wrong.

steps.rule: Real risk: errors, failed checks, actions that cannot be undone. The top of the urgency order. Overuse wears it out.
